<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-freshwater-fish" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-freshwater-fish-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of freshwater fish, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>160</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Garofalo et al. 2025</td><td>2</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Olmedo et al. 2013</td><td>2</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for freshwater fish, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/garofalo2025-seafood-cd-pb-hg-italy-10yr" class="internal" data-slug="sources/garofalo2025-seafood-cd-pb-hg-italy-10yr" data-no-cite-meta>Garofalo et al. 2025</a></li><li><a href="../sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Olmedo et al. 2013</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach freshwater Fish

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach freshwater Fish comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Freshwater Fish, as sold from lipid-soluble had dimethylarsinic acid higher at 200 µg/kg, against 20 µg/kg for lipid-soluble in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, freshwater Fish, as sold from Al Khawd (industrial area) (industrial-affected area) had lead higher at 159 µg/kg, against 20 µg/kg for Surur (control area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aljufaili2024-garra-shamal-oman|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Jufaili S, Al Khamisi S, Al Busaidi M, Al Habsi S · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aljufaili2024-garra-shamal-oman">Heavy metals in Garra shamal freshwater fish from Oman: accumulation and health risk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aljufaili2024-garra-shamal-oman">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that freshwater Fish, as sold from Rönnskär (polluted brackish water) (industrial-affected area) had total arsenic higher at 210 µg/kg, against 50 µg/kg for Bodaträsk (polluted fresh water) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/norin1985-swedish-fish-arsenic-speciation|22]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Norin H, Vahter M, Christakopoulos A, Sandstrom M · 1985</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/norin1985-swedish-fish-arsenic-speciation">Concentration of inorganic and total arsenic in fish from industrially polluted water</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemosphere</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/norin1985-swedish-fish-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Freshwater Fish, cooked (5 city composites) had lead lower at 9.9 µg/kg, against 14.3 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (freshwater fish, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

Risk assessment for the consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Reporting limits for total arsenic ranged from 0.159 µg/kg (Olmedo et al. 2013) to 300 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals|23]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Olmedo P, Pla A, Hernandez AF, Barbier F, Ayouni L, Gil F · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals">Determination of toxic elements (mercury, cadmium, lead, tin and arsenic) in fish and shellfish samples. Risk assessment for the consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

A useful lot result names the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below the limit that applies.

<a id="what-remains-unresolved-when-was-each-answer-reviewed-and-what-changed-in-this-version"></a>

Every source record that names freshwater Fish was decided on its content: 77 occurrence extracted, 77 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Freshwater Fish FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-freshwater-fish" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-freshwater-fish" data-question="What heavy metals are found in freshwater Fish?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in freshwater Fish?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, arsenic, total mercury, methylmercury, mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ag, As, As(V), AsB, Ba, BTs_sum, DBT, DOT, DPT, I, Li, MBT, Mo, MPT, oAs, OTC_sum_as_Sn, PTs_sum, Sr, sum of As species, sumOTC, TBT, TMA, TPhT and TPT in freshwater Fish, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-freshwater-fish" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-freshwater-fish" data-question="How do heavy metals get into freshwater Fish?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into freshwater Fish?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, freshwater Fish from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than freshwater Fish from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aljufaili2024-garra-shamal-oman|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Jufaili S, Al Khamisi S, Al Busaidi M, Al Habsi S · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aljufaili2024-garra-shamal-oman">Heavy metals in Garra shamal freshwater fish from Oman: accumulation and health risk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aljufaili2024-garra-shamal-oman">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Freshwater Fish, as sold from Al Amarat (industrial area) (industrial-affected area) had lead higher at 82 µg/kg, against 20 µg/kg for Surur (control area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aljufaili2024-garra-shamal-oman|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Jufaili S, Al Khamisi S, Al Busaidi M, Al Habsi S · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aljufaili2024-garra-shamal-oman">Heavy metals in Garra shamal freshwater fish from Oman: accumulation and health risk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aljufaili2024-garra-shamal-oman">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-freshwater-fish" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-freshwater-fish" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in freshwater Fish?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in freshwater Fish?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, freshwater Fish, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (3 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (100 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in WPRO (7.5 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (22.8 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-freshwater-fish" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-freshwater-fish" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in freshwater Fish?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in freshwater Fish?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same freshwater Fish.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Freshwater Fish, cooked (5 city composites) had lead lower at 9.9 µg/kg, against 14.3 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (freshwater fish, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-freshwater-fish-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-freshwater-fish-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in freshwater Fish is inorganic?">
